headline: Students block Awami League's return in Dhaka protest
summary: The Bangladesh Student Rights Council held a rally and procession to demand justice for July victims and prevent the banned party's political comeback.
details: The Bangladesh Student Rights Council organized a protest rally and procession on Saturday afternoon at the Raju Sculpture of Dhaka University as part of the July remembrance program.
The protesters demanded the trial of those responsible for disappearances, killings, and genocide, and called for the execution of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina according to court rulings.
Nazmul Hasan, central president of the council and a coordinator of the July uprising, stated that there is no place for Sheikh Hasina in Bangladesh following the 2024 uprising.
He urged Awami League leaders who were not involved in killings or lootings to accept the 'July' events to find justice.
Sadman Abdullah, the DU branch president of the council, warned against attempts to bring the Awami League back into the country, citing rumors of Sheikh Hasina's return in December.
The protesters also demanded that the government immediately implement the 'verdict of the July uprising' and launch the proposed July Memorial Museum by the end of the month.
Newaj Khan Bappi, senior vice president of the council, claimed that Awami League activists are organizing processions under the guise of food distribution programs in exchange for money.
caption:
Students in Dhaka rally to prevent the banned Awami League from returning to politics.

The Bangladesh Student Rights Council organized a protest rally and procession on Saturday afternoon at the Raju Sculpture of Dhaka University as part of the July remembrance program.

The protesters demanded the trial of those responsible for disappearances, killings, and genocide, and called for the execution of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina according to court rulings.

Nazmul Hasan, central president of the council and a coordinator of the July uprising, stated that there is no place for Sheikh Hasina in Bangladesh following the 2024 uprising.

He urged Awami League leaders who were not involved in killings or lootings to accept the 'July' events to find justice.

Sadman Abdullah, the DU branch president of the council, warned against attempts to bring the Awami League back into the country, citing rumors of Sheikh Hasina's return in December.

The protesters also demanded that the government immediately implement the 'verdict of the July uprising' and launch the proposed July Memorial Museum by the end of the month.

Newaj Khan Bappi, senior vice president of the council, claimed that Awami League activists are organizing processions under the guise of food distribution programs in exchange for money.

headline: World Cup: England and Norway tied 1-1 at halftime
summary: Andreas Sheldrup gave Norway the lead, but Jude Bellingham equalized for England in stoppage time of the first half.
details: England and Norway ended the first half of their World Cup quarter-final clash tied 1-1 at Miami Stadium.
Norway took the lead in the 36th minute when Andreas Sheldrup scored with a powerful shot that hit the far post and went into the net.
England dominated possession from the start, with Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham leading the attack, but struggled to break through initially.
Just as Norway seemed set to lead at the break, Jude Bellingham equalized in the second minute of added time, following an assist from Anthony Gordon.
If the match remains tied after regulation time, it will proceed to extra time and potentially a penalty shootout to decide the winner.
caption:
A World Cup quarter-final thriller! England and Norway are locked in a 1-1 stalemate after the first half.

England and Norway ended the first half of their World Cup quarter-final clash tied 1-1 at Miami Stadium.

Norway took the lead in the 36th minute when Andreas Sheldrup scored with a powerful shot that hit the far post and went into the net.

England dominated possession from the start, with Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham leading the attack, but struggled to break through initially.

Just as Norway seemed set to lead at the break, Jude Bellingham equalized in the second minute of added time, following an assist from Anthony Gordon.

If the match remains tied after regulation time, it will proceed to extra time and potentially a penalty shootout to decide the winner.
